about: Held-out tasks on five open-source repositories (bench/holdout/SOURCES.md). Expected findings were written from the ADR text and, for audit tasks, from an npm resolution worked out without decisis, before compare was run on these tasks. A decision that names the queried path itself is a path of one node: [decision]. Tasks marked 'text only' expect a decision that governs the path by its text but names no path, so no method that matches code paths can find it.

methods.A: Vinc retrieval only: nodes whose code_ref matches the subject, then their one-hop neighbours
methods.B: A plus the lockfile and the advisories as flat records joined by package name
methods.C: A Relate graph of the Vinc snapshot, the lockfile and the advisories, queried with multi-hop paths

tasks.subject: command/v7/create_org_command.go
tasks.connection: zero hops: two ADRs name command/v7, the directory that holds the file
tasks.why: ADR 11 sets the rules for the command layer under command/v7; ADR 12 decides that command/v7 is to be de-versioned. ADR 7 names only the test file, not this one.

tasks.subject: command/v7/create_org_command_test.go
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 7 names the file, ADRs 11 and 12 name its directory
tasks.why: ADR 7 uses this command test as its example of white box tests at the command level; ADRs 11 and 12 govern command/v7 as above.

tasks.subject: actor/v7action/droplet.go
tasks.connection: zero hops for ADR 12; ADR 11 calls the directory action/v7action, which does not exist (the code is in actor/v7action)
tasks.why: ADR 11's actor layer rules govern this file by their text, but the ADR spells the directory action/; the hand-made mapping keeps the ADR's spelling, so no method can find ADR 11 here. ADR 12 names actor/v7action.

tasks.subject: api/cloudcontroller/ccv3/application.go
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 11 names api/cloudcontroller/ccv3
tasks.why: ADR 11 sets the API layer rules: one file per API resource in api/cloudcontroller/ccv3, one request per method.

tasks.subject: integration/v7/isolated/create_org_command_test.go
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 7 names the file, ADR 12 names integration/v7
tasks.why: ADR 7 puts black box tests at the integration level and names this test; ADR 12 decides integration/v7 becomes integration/tests.

tasks.subject: api/rancher/management/v3/cluster.go
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 9 (structured proxy types) names ./api/rancher
tasks.why: The proxy types under ./api/rancher carry kubebuilder annotations and generated deep copies by ADR 9. ADR 8 is about the import strategy that creates v3 clusters, not about the type definitions.

tasks.subject: internal/controllers/clusterctl/config.go
tasks.connection: zero hops for ADR 16, which names the file; ADR 12 governs the embedded default config by its text and names no path
tasks.why: ADR 16 decides how the embedded config.yaml (embedded via config.go) pins CAPI versions. ADR 12 decides that the default ConfigMap for clusterctl.yaml overrides is embedded into the release and managed by the ClusterctlConfig resource.

tasks.subject: internal/controllers/clusterctlconfig_controller.go
tasks.connection: text only: ADR 12 decides the ClusterctlConfig resource this controller reconciles, but names no code path
tasks.why: No mapping can anchor ADR 12 without inventing a path; listed to measure what ADR text governs beyond the paths it names.

tasks.subject: internal/controllers/import_controller.go
tasks.connection: text only: ADR 6 decides how the operator imports clusters and ADR 8 changes 'the current import controller logic'; neither names a path
tasks.why: Both decisions govern the import controller by their text; neither names a file or directory.

tasks.subject: pkg/server/auth/auth.go
tasks.connection: zero hops for ADR 15; ADR 15 supersedes ADR 5, one SUPERSEDES edge away
tasks.why: ADR 15 describes the current authentication strategy and names this file. ADR 5 is superseded by ADR 15 and no longer governs; a walk that ignores edge meaning returns it.

tasks.subject: cmd/gitops-server/cmd/cmd.go
tasks.connection: zero hops for ADR 15; the superseded ADR 5 is one SUPERSEDES edge away
tasks.why: ADR 15 names cmd.go as one of the places that use a raw, non-impersonated client. ADR 5 is superseded.

tasks.subject: buf.gen.yaml
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 2 names buf.gen.yaml
tasks.why: ADR 2 standardises request and response APIs on protobuf generated with buf from buf.gen.yaml.

tasks.subject: .github/workflows/release.yaml
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 16 links the release workflow
tasks.why: ADR 16 changes the release ordering so the GitHub release is published only after the container image is available.

tasks.subject: cmd/gitops/
tasks.connection: text only: ADR 11 (verb noun) decides the CLI syntax and supersedes ADR 3 (noun verb), with the spelling 'Supercedes'; neither names a path
tasks.why: The gitops CLI under cmd/gitops follows ADR 11. ADR 3 is superseded; its status line says 'Superceded by', which decisis does not read as superseded.

tasks.subject: src/lib/auth.ts
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 1 names the file as the bespoke session system it replaces
tasks.why: ADR 1 adopts Auth.js v5 with the Prisma adapter and supersedes the session system in src/lib/auth.ts.

tasks.subject: prisma/schema.prisma
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 1 names prisma/schema.prisma
tasks.why: Under ADR 1, Auth.js owns the Account, Session and VerificationToken models in the schema. ADR 2 decides the system database topology, not the schema file.

tasks.subject: src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 1 names src/app/api/auth/{login,...}, a directory that holds the route
tasks.why: The login route is part of the bespoke auth that ADR 1 replaces with Auth.js.

tasks.subject: deploy/coolify/
tasks.connection: zero hops: ADR 3 lists deploy/coolify/ as related
tasks.why: ADR 3 decides one shared infrastructure plane with per-tenant databases; the Coolify template deploys it.

tasks.subject: src/auth.ts
tasks.connection: text only: src/auth.ts configures NextAuth with the Prisma adapter, which ADR 1 adopts; ADR 1 does not name this file
tasks.why: ADR 1 governs the Auth.js configuration by its text, but names only the files it replaces.

tasks.subject: src/index.ts
tasks.connection: text only: ADR 2 (TypeScript only) and ADR 3 (100% coverage for all source code) govern every source file and name none
tasks.why: Both decisions hold for all source code in the project; no ADR in this repository names a path.
